EB-05 “Heroines Edition vol.2”: official product facts and data limits

Research and data: OP Box Index · Published July 17, 2026 · Updated August 10, 2026 · Data sources & methodology

Bandai's official English product page confirms EB-05 as the second Heroines Extra Booster, with an October 2026 release window, USD $4.99 pack price, and 12 cards per pack. The same page does not yet publish an exact day, total card count, full card list, or Japanese display specification. This guide keeps those missing fields open instead of filling them with retailer assumptions.

Source checked August 10, 2026: Bandai's official EB-05 product page. Exact-day retailer listings are not treated as official confirmation.

Confirmed information and open fields

The official page establishes the product name, October release month, English pack price, and 12-card pack contents. It also describes EB-05 as the second Heroines Extra Booster. It does not provide a rarity breakdown, card-type total, exact English release day, or a Japanese-language product specification as of the review date.

Those gaps matter for sealed-box research. English pack contents cannot be copied into a Japanese display entry, and an exact date shown by a shop can change before Bandai updates its own product page. OP Box Index therefore labels the month as confirmed and the remaining fields as pending.

What EB-03 can and cannot tell us

EB-03 Heroines Edition is the closest thematic comparison because it is the first product in the same named line. Its live page contains the current sealed-box observations and chase-card data. Keeping that changing data on the EB-03 page avoids freezing an old price into this preview.

One predecessor is a sample of one. Differences in card list, print volume, distribution, release timing, and reprints can produce a different result for EB-05. EB-03's history is useful context, but it is not evidence that EB-05 demand or price will follow the same path.

Evidence required before a sealed-box valuation

A useful EB-05 valuation needs the official Japanese and English specifications, confirmed card list and treatments, language-matched completed sales, transaction counts, and a clear seal condition. Active listings may show seller expectations, but they are not substituted for sales. Card prices also do not automatically equal sealed-box value because pull rates and hit distribution must be known.

Reprint information is reported only when Bandai, distributors, or dated market supply records support it. Absence of a reprint notice is not described as proof that no reprint will occur.

How to verify a Japanese sealed display

For a Japanese One Piece display, require clear photos of the original Bandai security tape and confirm that it is uncut. Added shrink does not replace the tape check. Inspect the box code, top and bottom panels, side seams, dents, tears, and any adhesive irregularity. Loose packs, opened displays, mixed-language lots, and listings that conceal the tape are excluded.

The official English page describes packs, not a Japanese display seal. Product language and seal standard must therefore be recorded separately rather than inferred from the Heroines name.

Update policy

This page will be reviewed when Bandai publishes additional specifications, the card list appears, or a valid sold-box sample forms. Material changes receive a new visible review date. Price, population, and reprint fields follow the definitions in our methodology; unavailable values remain unavailable.

Frequently asked questions

When does EB-05 release?

Bandai's official English page lists October 2026. It did not list an exact day when checked on August 10, 2026.

What is the official English pack price?

Bandai lists USD $4.99 per pack, with 12 cards in an English pack.

How many card types are in EB-05?

The official page checked on August 10 did not list a total card-type count or full card list.

Does EB-03 predict EB-05's sealed-box price?

No. EB-03 is a relevant thematic comparison, but one predecessor cannot establish EB-05 demand, supply, or future price.

What seal should a Japanese EB-05 display have?

Use the original uncut Bandai security tape as the primary factory-seal check. Do not use added shrink as a substitute.
